replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics was never my strong suit. My vocational training focused on practical skills, and while I appreciate its importance, I prefer subjects like physics and history. I struggle with abstract concepts, so I avoid complex math when possible.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Not really anxious, but I do feel a sense of discomfort. Math wasn't a focus in my education, so when faced with equations, I feel out of my depth. It’s not a fear, just a lack of confidence due to limited exposure.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I tried an AI calculator app once to check some basic equations. It was user-friendly, but I didn’t explore advanced features. It helped, but I still prefer asking for help from colleagues when needed. I didn’t use it much beyond that.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write it in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / 2a. Calculate discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real roots. If zero, one root. If negative, complex roots. Plug values back into formula.

Find the first derivative f’(x). Set it equal to zero to locate critical points. Solve for x. Verify these points by checking the second derivative f''(x). If f''(x) > 0, it’s a minimum. If f''(x) < 0, it’s a maximum. If f''(x) = 0, test further or it’s an inflection point.
